ads_ratio.reason: Direct-listed ordinary (common) shares on both exchanges, so per-share figures from the filings and the NYSE price are on the same share basis: ratio 1.0.
ads_ratio.source: Fortis Inc. Form 40-F / FY2025 annual report: the Corporation's common shares are listed directly on the TSX and NYSE under the symbol FTS (release header: TSX/NYSE: FTS); there is no depositary or ADS program — the NYSE line is the same common shares.

moat_against: Returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs — no pricing power; FERC's Oct 2024 MISO base ROE decision cut ITC earnings retroactively ($20M hit to 2024)
Regulatory lag: costs of rate-base growth not yet in customer rates already pressure UNS Energy earnings
Heavy leverage (net debt $24.47B per dcf_numbers.json) and rate-sensitive funding costs
Perpetual equity issuance via the dividend reinvestment plan dilutes share count (~+1.7%/yr share CAGR in the engine blend)
Political/regulatory exposure across many jurisdictions plus CAD/USD translation exposure
moat_for: Regulated franchise monopolies — exclusive electric/gas service territories across five Canadian provinces, ten U.S. states and the Caribbean
Visible rate-base growth: $28.8B 2026-2030 capital plan driving ~7% midyear rate-base CAGR ($42.4B 2025 to $57.9B 2030 guided)
Diversification across 10 utilities and multiple regulators — no single rate case decides the company
52 consecutive years of common dividend increases; 4-6% annual dividend growth guided through 2030
Essential-service demand with low cyclicality; earnings grew through rate-base additions in 2025 and H1 2026
moat_justification: Regulated franchise monopolies across 10 North American utility subsidiaries (ITC transmission, UNS Energy, Central Hudson, FortisBC, FortisAlberta, Newfoundland Power et al.) give durable, regulator-granted exclusivity and a visible rate-base growth runway ($28.8B 2026-2030 capital plan, ~7% rate-base CAGR guided), but earned returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs, so there is no pricing power beyond the allowed return and regulators can and do reset returns downward (FERC's October 2024 MISO base ROE cut at ITC). That is a moderate/narrow moat: durable cash flows, capped economics.
name: Fortis Inc.
one_liner: High-quality regulated utility, moat 5/10, but owner's earnings are negative in every filed year (capex for rate-base growth runs well ahead of operating cash flow) — no positive normalized OE, so it cannot clear any hurdle on this model; Tier F by construction, confidence low (utility sector-model mismatch).

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine's sanity band anchors on the last FILED SBC value and Fortis has never filed an SBC value under any tag companyfacts carries (last_filed_value is null), so no in-band value exists. The C$150M is not an estimate — it is the sum of the two compensation-expense figures Fortis itself disclosed in Note 20 of its FY2025 financial statements (PSU C$109M + RSU C$41M).
sbc_override.reason: EDGAR companyfacts carries no SBC figure for Fortis under any candidate tag (ShareBasedCompensation, AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, ifrs AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments) for any filed year — sbc_tag is blank for 2016-2025 — so the v5 data gate gaps SBC for FY2023-2025. Fortis discloses the expense only in Note 20 of its financial statements. A single override value fills every untagged year, so the latest filed year (FY2025, C$150M) is used for all years: it overstates FY2024 (disclosed total C$82M = PSU C$53M + RSU C$29M), i.e. it errs in the conservative direction (more SBC = lower owner's earnings), and the amount is immaterial against the deeply negative OE base either way.
sbc_override.source: Fortis Inc. FY2025 consolidated financial statements (filed with the Form 40-F for the year ended Dec 31, 2025), Note 20 Stock-Based Compensation Plans: PSU compensation expense recognized C$109M (2025) and RSU compensation expense recognized C$41M (2025); DSU expense stated not material; stock options fully vested at Dec 31, 2025 with no expense figure disclosed. Total disclosed stock-based compensation expense FY2025 = C$150M (CAD, as filed; the engine FX-converts at period-end rates).
